1.explanation: This script stands up a minimal HTTP server that serves an HTML page embedding a cross-origin iframe (https://example.com).  It connects to Chrome over the DevTools Protocol, enables Network on the main target, then calls Target.setDiscoverTargets so it hears when Chrome spins up an OOPIF.  On each Target.targetCreated of type “iframe” it attaches to that targetId (getting a sessionId) and issues Network.enable over that new session.  You’ll see two classes of request URLs printed: the main page’s and the iframe’s.  Lighthouse’s current driver only calls Network.enable once on the main session and never attaches to the iframe session, so it never sees the OOPIF network events.  This script reproduces the pattern DevTools uses to work around the issue.
1.bug_scenario: When a page contains a cross-origin iframe that Chrome spins up in a separate process (an “OOPIF”), Lighthouse’s driver only enables the Network domain on the main target session.  In contrast, DevTools listens for Target.targetCreated, calls Target.attachToTarget on the new session, and then issues Network.enable over that session so it sees the iframe’s requests.  The bug images show DevTools issuing multiple Target.sendMessageToTarget calls (one for each sessionId, including the OOPIF) but Lighthouse’s gatherer never discovers or attaches to those extra targets and so never receives the Network.requestWillBeSent events from the iframe’s process.
